Description:
This RFP is an invitation by the Toronto Zoo to prospective suppliers to submit Bids for Construction Management for Services and Construction of the Conservation Campus.

The term of the agreement is to be for a period of thirty (30) months, with an option in favour of the Zoo to extend the term on the same terms and conditions for an additional term of up to six (6) months.

The Conservation Campus will be a cultural, institutional and tourism type of facility.

The two-building, two and one-storey, animal exhibit project is currently being designed by the Prime Consultant. 

Architecture

  1. The two-storey building will be primarily post-secondary teaching classrooms and laboratory (wet and dry) classrooms; and
  2. The one-storey building will be administration and retail spaces. It is at approximately 50% design development and enabling works are expected to take place in early 2023.
  3. The project integrates an animal exhibit within one of the proposed buildings and construction would abide by the Association of Zoos & Aquariums (“AZA”) guidelines.

Coordinating Project with Operations

  1. Phasing within an ongoing operating environment will be critical to the success of this project to coordinate demolition, temporary facilities and new construction while maintaining a fully operational site. The project integrates an animal exhibit within one of the proposed buildings and construction would abide by AZA guidelines.

Welcome Area

  1. The existing front entrance of the Zoo, the Welcome Area or Welcome Centre, was designed and built as part of the original construction. Minor modifications have been made subsequently with the addition of the Greenhouse gift shop, the expansion of admission booths, and also landscape upgrades.
  2. The Conservation Campus will be a state-of-the-art community gathering point and shows the Toronto Zoo as a world-class institution in the zoo community. This major revitalization is pivotal to signify the guests’ arrival point to the largest zoo in Canada and to provide essential and compelling guest services. This area of the Zoo has a major impact on the guest perception as it is the first and last point that a guest sees during their visit. The new front entrance is to be welcoming, functional, and will leave a lasting impression on all. The Conservancy Campus will be active year-round during day and evenings. The design includes guest admissions, retail, an otter exhibit, office space, labs, classrooms, and guest washrooms.

Description:
1. PROJECT OVERVIEW
    1. Design-Builder Services
  1. The Design-Builder shall provide the following:
  1. Complete review and assessment of the greenhouse site including existing structures, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing components, flooring, and drainage as well as all supporting equipment, infrastructure and amenities required to support the design phase.
  2. Construction including all necessary labour, equipment, materials to complete the work of the Project as outlined in the approved construction drawings and specifications.
  3. Relevant professional services to support the Design-Builder in completing the Project such as:  civil engineering, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, etc., to undertake all aspects of assessment, design development, and construction of the Greenhouse Retrofit Project. Attachment 1 shows the proposed greenhouse retrofit area.
    1. Project Objectives 
      1. The Greenhouse Retrofit project will revitalize the greenhouse areas to provide year-round access and viewing for Zoo guests. Currently, only one (1) of the three (3) greenhouses is accessible to guests, while the other two (2) are not. The retrofit will provide Zoo guests with access to all three (3) greenhouses including full accessibility, and significant guest/community engagement opportunities.
      2. With the addition of barrier-free entrances, 4-season vestibules, unobstructed floors with drains, HVAC systems/components, roof structures, electrical and lighting, hydroponic and water conservation technology and educational interpretive graphics, the Zoo's greenhouses will become world-class growing and teaching spaces.
      3. This new space for guests will be memorable and unique, providing measurable social and economic benefits through guest satisfaction, attendance, and revenue. It will provide the opportunity to expand engagement with the community, and horticultural enthusiasts.
      4. Timelines
        1. Assessment and design are expected to be undertaken in early-November 2022 and proceed as fast as possible.
        2. Construction is anticipated to begin in mid-November and be completed by early Summer 2023.
        3. The greenhouse is divided into three (3) sections and a phased approach to construction should be considered.

Title: RFP-72 - MANAGEMENT CONSULTING SERVICES FOR PROJECT MANAGEMENT OFFICE (PMO) PROJECT

Description:
ELECTRICAL PANEL

  1. Contractor to supply and install four (4) 208V 30A 2P breakers, to match existing; the Zoo to approve prior to installation.

ELECTRICAL FEEDING

  1. Contractor to supply and install #10 AWG RW90 cable to feed new electrical items. All conduit to be minimum 3/4”. EMT conduit, when indoors; once the cable reaches the outdoor space, to be switched to PVC. Conduits to run along exterior concrete wall inside pens. Preference is to pass conduit through existing openings to avoid drilling through the existing structure (beams, caging, etc.). If drilling through the existing structure, the surrounding area must be treated, made safe, made good as required.
  2. All conduit in the yard space to be run along the mesh ceiling, to minimize the birds’ curiosity.

THERMOSTATS & SWITCHES.

  1. Supply/Install on/off switches that are compatible with the Zoo-supplied heaters and thermostats. Contractor to propose switches; Zoo to approve.
  2. Install (4) thermostats (Zoo supplied), PECO industrial coiled temperature controller model TF115-001, to be placed on a north wall; location TBD on site. Thermostat to be installed in a protective case, Zoo to supply.

HEATERS.

  1. Supply and install (2) 4"X3/16" flat bars per heater, bolted to existing horizontal tubes with (2) 3/8" bolts at each edge of flat bar. 1" clear from bottom and sides of flat bar.
  2. Install four (4) Bromic heaters, 3000W, 208V, model: BH0420031; refer to specs provided. Bolt brackets to flat bars or plywood, respectively. Heaters must be no less and no more than 5” from ceiling and no less than 72” from finished floor. Contractor to review and follow manufacturer requirements.
  3. Supply and install 1/2"x1/2" welded galvanized mesh as a heater cover/protection solution that will prevent the birds from perching on the heater. To be attached to ceiling chain-link and plywood. Must not have any sharp exposed ends.

HVAC

  1. Existing (4) duct branches at trunk to be dismantled & closed. See drawing A1.02, plan 1 to see which branches are to be closed.
  2. Supply and install new branches from existing trunk into the pens, perforating the existing mesh. Install and supply (2) duct flanges where duct intersects mesh. Mesh to be treated, enclosed around duct to made look good as required. New branches must be fastened to ceiling with straps & struts, to match existing ones. Branches must be aligned centered with yards’ doors. New branches inside pens must have bird spikes or bird-coil installed on-top to prevent birds from perching.
  3. Supply and install (2) 8" x 12" 200CFM diffuser at the end of each branch (8 diffusers total). One diffuser shall be placed facing down inside the pen, and the second shall be directed towards the yards. The end of the branch with the (2) diffusers shall be installed 1" from door frame & 8" from top of the door. See picture 3 on drawing A1.02, and section 1 on drawing A1.03.
  4. Supply and install standard dampers at the end of each branch, before the diffusers. The goal is to have the choice to redirect the airflow during the winter into the indoor pen, or out towards the outdoor yards.

GENERAL NOTES

  1. Heaters, thermostats and thermostat boxes supplied by the Zoo.
    1. Refer to specification sheets in bidding package.
  2. Contractor to adhere to Ontario Electrical Safety Code standard.
  3. Contractor to provide a certificate of inspection at completion of work.
  4. Contractor responsible for all necessary permits required by law, including but not limited to, ESA.

Tentative Schedule

  1. Work only from 7:30 AM to 5:00 PM on Working Days, unless otherwise specified by the Zoo, continuously to minimize exhibit downtime and disturbing guest experience.
  2. Provide a Detailed Construction Schedule to Zoo within five (5) Working Days after award in a satisfactory format. The Schedule shall reflect completion of work within the specified time in accordance with the drawings and specifications herein.
  3. If Contractor desires a major change in method of operation after commencing construction, or if actual progress is straying from the Schedule, submit a Revised Detailed Schedule for approval prior to beginning revised operation.
  4. Project Completed: 2024-11-01.

Description:
Construction Manager

This NRFP is to source and retain a qualified Construction Manager (“CM”) to work under the direction of the Toronto Zoo’s Project Manager on the Conservation Centre project, and to act as the Prime Contractor for the project.

Conservation Centre Project

Architecture

  1. The new two-building, animal exhibit and interior renovations for the existing Membership Building Project (the “Project”) is currently being designed by Zeidler Architecture Inc. (the “Consultant”).

    1. The two-storey building will be primarily post-secondary teaching classrooms and laboratory (wet and dry) classrooms; and

    2. The one-storey building will be administration and retail spaces. It is at approximately 100% design development and enabling works are expected to take place in early 2023.

    3. The new buildings will be targeting net zero emissions as per City of Toronto requirements.

    4. Renovation work required to “make good” the existing Membership Building, related to proposed demolition as indicated in the NRFP documents.

  2. Coordinating Project with Operations

    1. Phasing within an ongoing operating environment will be critical to the success of this Project to coordinate demolition, temporary facilities and new construction while maintaining a fully operational site. The Project integrates an animal exhibit within one of the proposed buildings and construction would abide by the AZA guidelines.

  3. Zoo Welcome Area

    1. The existing front entrance of the Zoo was designed and built as part of the original construction. Minor modifications have been made subsequently with the addition of the Greenhouse gift shop, the expansion of admission booths, and also landscape upgrades.

    2. The Conservation Centre will be a state-of-the-art community gathering point and shows the Toronto Zoo as a world-class institution in the zoo community. This major revitalization is pivotal to signify the guests’ arrival point to the largest zoo in Canada and to provide essential and compelling guest services. This area of the Zoo has a major impact on the guest perception as it is the first and last point that a guest sees during their visit. The new front entrance is to be welcoming, functional, and will leave a lasting impression on all. The design includes guest admissions, retail, an otter exhibit, office space, labs, classrooms, and guest washrooms. The Conservation Centre will be active year-round and in the evenings.
